mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises real interest rates, reducing present value of future corporate earnings and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the median baseline at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure, compresses profit margins, and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by > 3% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the median baseline at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS over two months signals weakening housing demand and reduced household savings, which together depress consumer spending and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 0% MoM and RSAFS < 0% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the joint proxy condition fails to explain at least 10% of the variance in returns at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS above 0.4% and a decline in UNRATE below 5% for three consecutive months signals a labor market cooling within an expanding economy, which typically precedes a flattening earnings growth and results in muted S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.4% MoM and UNRATE < 5% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: transition from tight to loose labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from the overall median at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in FEDFUNDS below 1% during a period of negative GDP growth signals an emergency easing, which boosts risk appetite and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 1pp in one month and GDPC1 YoY < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized increase in CPIAUCSL above 4% for six consecutive months signals high inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% YoY for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the median baseline at 5% significance.
